Floor still 3 but the shape is new: every block-1 register seat now matches the target and only the D_800A3916 lbu slot (3 insns) remains; s1's whole 24-insn rotation family is explained by one predic

Floor still 3; read the sched1 trace directly and closed the block-1 dependence space - all five ways to stall T-3 are now measured dead, and the only register-consistent one is blocked by local-alloc

frontier.hypothesis: The residual is now a pure RA question with a fully specified goal: on the z0/v3b shape (correct instruction order, 24 seat insns) make global_alloc give reg 74 - a pseudo with two disjoint live ranges and 12 references in block 1 - the $v0 seat, i.e. ensure no block-1 local quantity holds $v0 across 74's span.
frontier.mechanism: local_alloc (local-alloc.c:471) runs first and can only be denied a register by removing the quantity or by changing its conflict set; global_alloc's find_reg then picks from what is left. The solver models both passes exactly, so this is a REACHABLE/FORECLOSED question rather than a spelling search.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/ra_solver/extract.py on code6cac_c_mid, then inverse.py / inverse_compose.py classify pinned to block 1 of the z0 body with the goal {74: $v0, 75: $a0}, and enumerate which live-range / quantity configurations are REACHABLE; spell only those. z0 is banked at rejected/flag-into-packed-2-deaths-forces-global-alloc-24.c and regenerable from tmp/grind/func_8003A728/s3/z0.c.

frontier.hypothesis: Changing the block-1 INSN SET (one more or one fewer instruction), rather than the dependence carrier, changes either the T-2 ready list or the local-quantity ordering and opens the stall.
frontier.mechanism: The five-arrangement closure and the T-2 pin are both statements about the CURRENT insn set of block 1; sched.c's ready lists and local-alloc.c's quantity order are both functions of that set. s2 measured that moving one statement (`hi16 = D_800A37C4 << 16;`) alone spans 14/10/6/3/14, so the block is highly sensitive to its own composition.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate legitimate re-associations of the packed expression and of the two `D_800A3698` / `D_800A369C` stores that add or remove exactly one block-1 insn (e.g. hoisting the `buf8 & 0xFFFF` sub-expression into an explicit local that the later `func_8003A6FC` arms also read - the target computes it once into $s2 - or splitting the `(vsync << 31) | (D_800A3730 << 30)` pair), and measure each with sandbox; re-read the .sched trace whenever the T-2 ready list changes.

frontier.hypothesis: The buf8 low-half reuse carried since s1 (writing the `(u16)D_800A3698` / `(u16)D_800A36D0` loads into the existing call-crossing `buf8` local) still needs its family decided before any candidate-ready submission; every other construct in the candidate is ordinary C.
frontier.mechanism: Policy, not codegen: the reuse is either ordinary step-wise scratch-variable C (the matched sibling func_8003A5A0 in the same TU uses the same idiom) or the staged-value-reused-variable family, which mandates a /* FAKE */ annotation plus documented lever exhaustion.
frontier.next_probe: Grep docs/reference/sotn-construct-index.md for a low-half-load-written-into-an-existing-call-crossing-local precedent (PSX/untagged entries only) BEFORE writing self_vet.md; if the census comes back negative, emit ruling-request rather than a submission.
